title: On-call & Incident Response - process, runbooks, postmortems, rotations, game days, status page & comms templates
author: Jordan Kim
content:
Summary:

This page documents Redwood Inference's official on-call and incident response program: severity definitions, roles and responsibilities, the incident lifecycle, canonical runbooks, postmortem expectations, on-call rotation rules, game day playbooks, and standardized status page / customer communications templates. It is intended for engineers, SREs, product managers, and customer-facing teams who participate in incident handling.

Scope and goals:
- Provide a single, reproducible process for detecting, escalating, responding to, and learning from incidents.
- Reduce time-to-detect (TTD) and time-to-recover (TTR) while maintaining blameless postmortems and clear customer communications.
- Ensure repeatable on-call schedules and handoffs so coverage is predictable across regions and services.

Incident severity matrix (quick reference):
- Sev0 (Critical): Complete outage or data loss affecting >20% of customers or business-critical telemetry (SLO breach imminent). Requires immediate page and executive notification. Target MTTR: <30 minutes.
- Sev1 (High): Major degradation for a significant subset of customers or sustained SLO breach. Page the on-call, target MTTR: <2 hours.
- Sev2 (Medium): Partial functionality loss or degraded performance for limited customers; no immediate SLO breach. Email/Slack escalation to on-call within 60 minutes.
- Sev3 (Low): Informational, minor errors, or feature requests; handled in normal sprint. No immediate paging.

Ownership & roles:
- Primary on-call (Responder): First responder for pages. Owns initial triage, mitigation, and status updates until handoff.
- Secondary on-call (Escalation): Backstop for primary; handles deep debugging and cross-service coordination.
- Incident Commander (IC): Assigned for Sev0/Sev1 incidents when cross-team coordination is required. Coordinates cross-functional teams, prioritizes actions, and owns customer comms cadence.
- Communications Lead (Comms): Prepares status page and external messages, liaises with Customer Success / Sales for high-impact incidents.
- Postmortem Author: Owner of the post-incident write-up (usually the IC or service owner).
- Engineering Manager / Team Lead: Approves mitigations requiring major rollout or rollback, and ensures postmortem follow-through.

Escalation matrix & on-call contact points:
1. Pager triggers -> Primary on-call Slack channel and PagerDuty page.
2. If primary does not acknowledge within 5 minutes for Sev0/Sev1 (10 minutes for Sev2), escalate to Secondary.
3. If unresolved after 30 minutes for Sev0 -> Page IC + Eng Director.
4. For customer-impacting incidents that persist >1 hour -> Notify Customer Success and Sales leadership.

Incident lifecycle (detailed steps):
1) Detection & Triage:
  - Alert fires to PagerDuty and on-call Slack.
  - Primary on-call acknowledges within 5 minutes (Sev0/Sev1) and posts initial triage to #incidents (include time, service, affected region, error rates, preliminary hypothesis).
  - Attach relevant dashboards and runbook links.
2) Mitigation & Containment:
  - Apply immediate mitigations from runbooks (e.g., scale up replica, restart worker pool, disable feature flag) to reduce impact.
  - If mitigation is temporary, document rollback criteria and follow-up plan.
3) Escalation & Coordination:
  - If mitigation fails within defined window, escalate to Secondary or IC.
  - IC opens incident channel (Slack huddle + Zoom if needed) and assigns roles (scribe, comms, triage leads).
4) Customer Communications:
  - Comms Lead publishes an initial status page message within 30 minutes for Sev0 and within 1 hour for Sev1. Use templates below.
  - Provide regular updates every 30 minutes for Sev0 and every hour for Sev1 until resolved.
5) Recovery & Validation:
  - Confirm systems are back to normal via metrics and synthetic checks.
  - Keep incident channel open for at least one SLO window to monitor for regressions.
6) Post-incident:
  - Postmortem drafted within 72 hours and completed/published within 7 business days.
  - Owner tracks action items with clear owners and deadlines.

Canonical runbook template (use for service-level incidents):
- Runbook title: <service-name> - <symptom>
- Preconditions: What must be true to run this (access, tool availability).
- Detection query / ALARM: Exact PromQL/ELK/KQL query or alert rule.
- Quick mitigation steps (ordered, with CLI examples):
  1. Identify affected instances: curl -s https://ops-api/services/<service>/instances | jq '.status'
  2. Restart workers: ./opsctl restart --service <service> --region us-west-2
  3. Scale up: kubectl scale deploy <deployment> --replicas=5 -n production
  4. Toggle feature flag: flagsctl set <flag> false --service <service>
- Validation checks: What dashboards/metric thresholds confirm mitigation.
- Escalation path: who to page if mitigation fails.
- Post-incident remediation checklist: config fixes, postmortem link, follow-up PRs.

Runbook maintenance and ownership:
- Each service must have a runbook owner listed in its README and in the runbook header.
- Runbooks reviewed quarterly. Missed reviews trigger an alert to team leads.

Postmortem template & expectations (blameless):
- Title: [SEV#] Short description (service - symptom)
- Incident window: start_time / end_time / total_duration
- Summary: 1-3 sentence high-level summary and customer impact.
- Timeline: Chronological events with timestamps (system events, alerts, human actions).
- Root cause(s): Technical explanation of the failure chain.
- Contributing factors: Process, monitoring gaps, flaky dependencies.
- Resolution & mitigation: What was done to stop the impact.
- Action items (owner, due date, status): Each must be small, testable, and tracked in JIRA.
- Metrics & impact: Affected customer count, SLO impact, error/token counts, cost impact if applicable.
- Follow-up verification plan: How we will validate the fix and prevent regression.
- Lessons learned & prevention roadmap.

On-call rotation policy (practical rules):
- Primary on-call shift length: 7 days by default (teams may adopt 1-week or 2-week rotations; documented on team page).
- Secondary on-call: overlapping one-week rotation, responsible for escalation.
- Weekends & holidays: volunteers prioritized; if not enough volunteers, manager assigns and compensatory time-off provided.
- Handoffs: Outgoing on-call must run a 30-minute synchronous handoff with incoming on-call at shift boundary (record a short written summary if asynchronous). Hand-off summary must include: current incidents, ongoing mitigations, unstable services, and upcoming maint windows.
- Time allowance for pager response: acknowledge within 5 minutes for Sev0/Sev1, 10 minutes for Sev2.
- On-call wellbeing: Protected time policy - no more than 2 consecutive on-call rotations without at least 1 week off.

Game days (practice incidents):
- Purpose: Validate runbooks, measure real TTR under deliberate failure, verify cross-team coordination, and surface monitoring gaps.
- Frequency: Quarterly per SRE/critical-service team; annual company-wide game day.
- Typical game day playbook:
  1. Define scope & blast radius (non-prod or isolated production subset).
  2. Run the failure (traffic shift, instance failure, network partition).
  3. Observe on-call response and time-to-detect.
  4. Debrief: 30-60 minute session to identify gaps and create follow-ups.
  5. Update runbooks and dashboards based on findings.

Status page & customer communications templates (copy/paste):
- Status page initial (Sev0):
  Title: Major outage impacting Redwood API - [region/service]
  Summary: We are investigating an issue affecting the Redwood API in <region>. Some requests are failing or experiencing high latency. Our on-call engineers are actively investigating.
  Impact: Request failures and high latency for a subset of customers in <region>.
  Next update: 30 minutes
- Status page update (progress):
  Title: Mitigation in progress - partial recovery observed
  Summary: We have applied a mitigation (scaled workers / rolled back recent deploy) and are seeing partial recovery. Traffic is being served at reduced capacity while we verify stability.
  Impact: Reduced errors; some customers may still experience timeouts.
  Next update: 30 minutes
- Status page resolution:
  Title: Incident resolved - service restored
  Summary: The Redwood API is operating normally. We will follow up with a postmortem and remediation plan.
  Impact: No ongoing customer impact.

Customer-facing Slack/email template (short):
- Subject: Incident update: Redwood API in <region> - [Investigating|Mitigating|Resolved]
- Body: Hello - We are currently investigating an issue impacting the Redwood API in <region>. Our engineers are working on a fix. We will provide updates every 30 minutes. If you are experiencing production impact, please reply to this message and include your customer ID. - Redwood Support

Internal incident communication checklist (IC/Comms):
- Post initial triage: create incident channel and pin runbook and dashboards.
- Publish first status update to status.redwood.ai within 30 minutes for Sev0.
- Notify Sales and Customer Success for any customer-reported impact.
- Record timeline entries in the incident doc as actions occur.
- Close incident when metrics and synthetic checks are stable for one SLO window.

SLOs, alerts and governance:
- Link to SLOs: teams must include SLO links in runbook headers.
- Alert tuning: false-positive rate target <5% monthly; escalate when alerts fire outside expected traffic patterns.
- Quarterly review: incident triage metrics (TTD, TTR, number of Sev1/Sev0) reviewed with leadership and used to prioritize reliability work.

Post-incident follow-up & tracking:
- Postmortem published within 7 business days and linked in the incident ticket.
- Action items with owners and deadlines added to JIRA and tracked through to completion before the postmortem is closed.
- Runbook updates scheduled as follow-ups from the postmortem.

Appendix: quick links & cheat sheet
- PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.redwood.example
- Status page editor: https://status.redwood.example/admin
- Runbook repo: https://git.redwood.example/runbooks
- Incident template (Google Doc): https://docs.redwood.example/incident-template

Revision history:
- 2026-01-30: Created by Jordan Kim.
- 2026-03-01: Minor clarifications to communication cadence and game day frequency (reviewers: Ava Chen, Marcus Lee).

If you have questions about this process or want to propose changes, please file a request in the #incidents-policy channel or contact the Eng SRE team.
